doc.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006

title: Twelve-tone practice as ear training
summary: Jordan practices atonal twelve-tone lines as ear training, but only plays what fits what he hears.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Exactly. And a lot of times a lot of my music sometimes is atonal. I use a twelve-tone system in some of my music. And I practice a lot of it. And you know my daughter always tells me, says, “Daddy you practice on that atonal music but I don’t hear it when it comes out on the records.” And I say, “cause they don’t line it up for me.” And then when she say, “you don’t ever play nothing you practice.” ‘Cause I’ve got some lines that I play on twelve-tone, twelve-tone lines that I can retrograde and do all of that but I try to keep them going and what have you when I’m playing. But if I’m not I haven’t got — sometimes they’ll set up something for me to hear. But just for me to do it like I practice it, I don’t ever do it. Because the way I practice it, for it to come out when it’s time for it to come out, if somebody hits something like that that sounds like that, then it will come out. But if they don’t ever do it then I won’t do it just ‘cause I know it. And my daughter, who studied classical music, always tells me that. Say, “why don’t I hear something that you’re practicing on?” And I say that’s just for ear training.
Right. I say that’s my ear training exercise.
Interesting. You said something just a second ago and I was trying to remember what it was, it’s something about I’m not going to play it just to play it, it’s got to fit.

That’s right. I got to hear it. I got to hear how it’s going to fit in a certain thing. And sometimes some of the licks, some of the things, like they say, “man you played that lick here and you played that lick there, because that same stimuli came over to me again and I heard that particular thing and it just jumped out without me having any control over it. You know? And like sometimes in minor keys and modes and some things, some stuff just, and, “man you know that’s awesome” and I say well it just came out.
